title: What Even Is Trading?
hook: Trading isn't predicting the future. You're participating in price movement.

launchpad.outcome: Explain what a trade actually is (market, direction, risk, outcome) before any strategy talk.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Is "I think price is going up" a complete trading plan?

stages.caption: Outcome: price moves, position gains or loses value.

slides.headline: Trading isn’t predicting.
slides.line: It’s taking a position because you expect price to move.

slides.headline: Up or down. You can trade both.

check.prompt: She expects MNQ to fall. Which side?

options.label: Long
options.feedback: Long profits when price rises. She expects it to fall.

options.label: Short
options.why: Short profits when price falls. Futures let you do either from your very first trade.

slides.headline: Your trade ticket.
slides.line: Tap each line to fill it in. Every trade you take has these four.

rows.label: Outcome
rows.value: Price moves. You gain or lose.

slides.headline: “I think price is going up.”
slides.line: Is that a trade? Tap what’s missing.
slides.presentNote: Direction is the one piece she does have. Look for what’s missing.
slides.why: Direction alone isn’t a plan. A trade needs all four: market, direction, risk and outcome.

cards.label: Trading
cards.sub: Profit from the move, over a much shorter window

check.prompt: You’re here to trade. So your job is…

options.label: To know exactly what happens next
options.feedback: Nobody knows that, and you don’t need to. Look again.

options.label: To read what price is showing you and follow your rules
options.why: Our job isn’t to know exactly what happens next. It’s to interpret what price is showing us and make rule-based decisions.

check.prompt: Price hit the spot your plan said you’re wrong. Now what?

options.label: Hold and hope it comes back
options.feedback: Waiting for the market to “prove you right” isn’t a risk plan.

options.label: Exit, like your plan says
options.why: A thesis can be reasonable and still be wrong. That’s why risk is defined before the trade, not decided emotionally after.

slides.line: Later, you’ll learn to build a thesis, wait for confirmation, and define exactly what would make that thesis invalid.

slides.prompt: Why isn’t “I think price is going up” a complete trading plan?
slides.modelAnswer: It only covers direction. It doesn’t say what market, how much risk, where you’d be proven wrong, or what the outcome plan is. A real trade needs all four pieces: market, direction, risk, and outcome.

takeaways: Trading is participating in price movement, not predicting the future.
Going long profits from price rising; going short profits from price falling.
Every trade has four pieces: market, direction, risk, and outcome.
remember: Trading isn't about being certain. It's about making structured decisions under uncertainty.
